cim: Data Centers: Benefits vs Costs and Risks
cim_eredeti: Data Centers: Benefits vs Costs and Risks
szoveg_eredeti:
The dramatic recent surge in investment in data centers in the United States is boosting the economy but at the same time sparking heated opposition. The stark tensions reflect very different viewpoints on the benefits vs the costs and risks of data centers. For their supporters, data centers are providing the infrastructure backbone for the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with a potentially transformative long-term impact on the US economy, well beyond the already significant short-term stimulus to growth. However, critics have raised a wide range of concerns: that the data center boom and the required massive debt financing needed to sustain it could end in a damaging bust; that the promised local benefits of data centers in terms of jobs and tax revenues are exaggerated while the spending on data centers is crowding out other types of investment; that data centers can impose heavy energy and environmental costs on local communities; and that the Artificial Intelligence that data centers are empowering will destroy jobs and even threaten humanity itself.

Greater realism about the costs and benefits of data centers is clearly required. While data center construction underpins the rollout of AI that could have a transformative impact on the US economy, a “full speed ahead” laissez faire policy on data center construction runs into serious concerns about the costs and risks involved. Moreover, such an approach is not politically feasible as the pressures on power supply costs have become better appreciated and the limited net benefits for most local community hosts more soberly assessed. Regaining popular support for data centers will depend on a better calibrated approach to meeting burgeoning power needs — ensuring that the costs of the needed increase in capacity fall squarely on the data center operators rather than on local electricity consumers and fostering the required growth of overall electric power capacity. It will also be important to develop partnerships between data center builders and local communities that provide greater transparency about decision-making and optimize local benefits. More broadly, at a national level, steps to ensure that the benefits of the AI rollout are more widely shared and that the costs and financial risks are adequately controlled would help to rebuild public support.
